messages:
maria: Seeing a pretty consistent p95 east-west jump during the 11:30-12:30 batching window in us-east-1. Baseline p95 ~8ms, spike to 120-180ms for ~8 mins at peak. GPU queues stall and we get soft-evictions. Anyone else seeing this?
ashwin: Yep, alerted. Digging into rdma/eth stats now. Quick look shows a burst of retransmits and some MLX5 "rqe_err" counters climbing at the same time.
maria: Packet loss + latency coincide with bigger batches starting at 11:28. Affected pods are on two adjacent racks (rack-a3 -> rack-a4).
ashwin: Ran a tcpdump capture on node-gpu-14, grabbing RDMA/UDPY traffic. Snippet:```17:28:12.345 IP node-gpu-14 > node-gpu-27: UDP, length 2048``` lots of retries after that. Also psm2_epstat shows handshake latency spikes: ```psm2_stats: connect_ms=120, retries=18```
noah: Could be jumbo frame mismatch or ToR MTU grooming. Last time we saw similar it was a partial MTU rollback during a switch upgrade. Any recent infra churn?
leo: Not that I'm aware of in that cluster. No scheduled ToR firmware pushes today. I can check switch logs though.
maria: k8s events show kubelet reported network flaps on a few nodes around the same time. No OOMs or CPU thundering.
ashwin: Ethtool counters from node-gpu-27 at spike time:```rx_errors: 12
tx_errors: 0
rx_missed: 6
mlx5_rqe_err: 9``` Also saw a flurry of NACKs in the RDMA logs.
leo: If rx_errors > 0 but tx_errors ~0 it smells like ingress shaping or buffer exhaustion on the receiving NIC or on the switch ASIC. Could be sudden fanout from batching causing per-queue saturation.
noah: Short term mitigation: can we rate-limit the batch fanout or reduce max_batch_tokens for the next peak? We can also pre-warm K/V caches so requests hit fewer nodes.
maria: Agree. I'll push a conservative throttle to batch_size_limit=0.7x for the 11:30 window and pre-warm shards. Who can validate the rollback when we finish window?
ashwin: I'll keep captures running and tail /var/log/kern.log for mlx5 messages. Also plan to enable per-port debug counters for next peak. Command I used:```ethtool -S ens4f0 | egrep 'rx_|tx_|rqe'```
leo: On the ops side I'll talk to the DC NOC to check ToR buffer drops and ECMP flap logs. Ask them to review recent QoS profile changes.
infra-bot: Incident alert created: INC-2024-0817-eastwest-latency. Pager duty notified.
maria: Update after first throttle: we saw p95 drop back to ~15-20ms within ~90s of applying throttle. Not perfect but huge improvement. No evictions in the last 20m.
noah: Good quick win. Long term we should: 1) validate MTU end-to-end (jumbo frames enabled and consistent), 2) coordinate a NIC firmware bump (mlx5 fw known issue w/ rqe hysteresis), 3) consider shaping at the ToR for large fanout flows, 4) add batching-slowstart to spread fanout ramp.
ashwin: I'll open a follow-up ticket with captures and `psm2`/`ibv_devinfo` outputs. Early suspicion: RDMA handshake backoff combined with buffer exhaustion on ingress queues.
maria: Thanks. Action items: ashwin -> post capture + psm2 stats (ETA 2h), leo -> NOC check + ToR logs (ETA 3h), noah -> perf change proposal for batching-slowstart (ETA EOD). I'll keep the temporary throttle in place for next 48h.
noah: +1. Also let's add a Canary to avoid full-cluster burst when we revert throttle.
leo: Noted. NOC already found a microcode bump attempt last week that partially failed on a subset of ToRs; they're correlating.
maria: Perfect. If anyone sees a re-spike ping @maria directly. Thanks all :thumbsup:
